name: Sterol Metabolism Disorder with Epilepsy
aliases: Inherited Sterol Metabolism Defect with Seizures

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Sterol Metabolism Disorder with Epilepsy

criteria.description: Elevated plasma or tissue sterol intermediates detected by mass spectrometry
Presence of recurrent epileptic seizures confirmed by EEG
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sterol metabolism
Presence of characteristic facial or skeletal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biochemical abnormality, epileptic seizures, and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data.

searchTerms: high blood levels of cholesterol precursor

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distinctive facial dysmorphism including micrognathia and broad nasal bridge
searchTerms: distinct facial features with small chin
wide nose bridge and small jaw
unusual face shape with broad nose and small lower jaw

common.symptomName: Developmental delay with impaired motor milestones
Intellectual disability ranging from mild to severe
searchTerms: learning difficulties from mild to severe
failure to gain weight as baby

occasional.symptomName: Ocular abnormalities including cataracts or nystagmus
searchTerms: eye problems like cataracts or eye shaking
cloudy eye lens or involuntary eye movements

occasional.symptomName: Skeletal abnormalities such as scoliosis or joint contractures
Behavioral disturbances including hyperactivity or autistic features

searchTerms: tube feeding due to swallowing issues

laboratory: Elevated plasma and tissue sterol intermediates (e.g., 7-dehydrocholesterol)
Elevated liver enzymes in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination
Skeletal X-rays revealing bone dysplasia or scoliosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding enzymes of the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway (e.g., DHCR7 mutations)
other: Characteristic facial dysmorphism documented by clinical photography

distinguishingFeatures: Similar sterol metabolism defect but with more pronounced congenital malformations
Different genetic mutations unrelated to sterol metabolism

redFlags: Early onset refractory seizures unresponsive to standard antiepileptic drugs
Presence of biochemical sterol abnormalities in plasma or tissues
